content.objective: [PLACEHOLDER] Locate and read a real responsible disclosure or bug bounty policy from a major technology company, and identify the key rules that define legal and authorised security research.
instructions: [PLACEHOLDER] Open your web browser and navigate to a well-known technology company — for example Google, Microsoft, GitHub, or Cloudflare.
[PLACEHOLDER] Search their website for a 'Responsible Disclosure Policy', 'Security Policy', or 'Bug Bounty Program' page. You can also search: site:company.com responsible disclosure
[PLACEHOLDER] Read through the policy and note: (1) what is explicitly in scope, (2) what is explicitly out of scope, and (3) what you are NOT allowed to do.
[PLACEHOLDER] Write down one thing that surprised you about the policy — something you did not expect to be allowed or forbidden.
successCriteria: [PLACEHOLDER] You found a published responsible disclosure or bug bounty policy from a real company.
[PLACEHOLDER] You can name at least one activity the policy explicitly permits.
[PLACEHOLDER] You can name at least one activity the policy explicitly forbids.
content.reflection: [PLACEHOLDER] Why do companies publish responsible disclosure policies? What does it tell you about the relationship between security researchers and the organisations they help?
